summary: iter459 backend regression pass for the buyer payment-letter accuracy fix. Ran the iter459 dataset pytest (7/7 PASS), iter459 live E2E buyer payment-letter verifier against the live preview backend (51/51 PASS covering EN+FR PDFs for Buyer A and Buyer B, exclusion of Buyer B's lots + unsold lot from Buyer A's letter, real paddle 12001/12002, real BP 5.00% = $6.05, real Stripe recovery, real GST 5.0% + QST 9.975% tax lines, French labels 'Prime d'acheteur' / 'Total marteau' / 'TPS' / 'TVQ'), plus a full sibling regression sweep: iter451 hammer_total (36/36 PASS), iter457 seller-docs accuracy pytest (5/5) + live seller statement / seller receipt / commission invoice (all 200s with real buyer names, real paddles, real commission%, real GST/QST), iter458 tax-label live (all provinces GST/QST/HST correct EN+FR, no synthesised PST/TVP), iter451 lots-won invoice EN+FR live E2E (line totals, hammer total, unit prices, qty all correct). Fee engine + tax engine + hammer resolver produce identical outputs to iter458 (no engine files modified). No regressions detected in any unrelated invoice endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: Helper `_build_settled_buyer_dataset` correctly delegates all fee/tax math to services.fee_calculator.calculate_fee and unit×qty math to services.hammer_total.resolve_hammer_total — no local recomputation, no placeholder data. Good separation of concerns.
PDF template only renders engine outputs (never recalculates) — aligns with the mandatory rule in the review request.
400 raised when a user has zero won lots — prevents empty/placeholder letters from being generated. Correct behavior.
Paddle lookup returns None when absent instead of inventing a fake paddle — correct; route layer handles minting. No regression risk on downstream docs.
